Cost claims differ: $222 million (utility releases; SPP IEP Table 3 gives Proposal B's RFP Response Estimate as $222,551,930) versus SPP's study cost estimate of $423,983,009. All figures cover the whole two-segment project, not only the Texas segment.

evidence.supports: one continuous line from Potter to Beckham

evidence.exactExcerpt: The Project involves a proposed 15‑mile, 345‑kilovolt (kV) electric transmission line extending from the Oklahoma state line to the Beckham Substation in Beckham County, Oklahoma.
evidence.supports: the Oklahoma segment begins at the state line

evidence.exactExcerpt: upon the OCC's route review and approval, one route is built based on public feedback and feasibility. NO FINAL LINE ROUTE HAS BEEN DETERMINED.

unresolved: No PUCT docket was found for the SPS Texas segment as of 2026-09-26. Xcel lists a PUCT CCN in its permit table (xcel-potter-beckham-siting p.2), and routing and siting studies are scheduled through Q4 2026, so a CCN application is probably not yet filed. This could not be confirmed: a web search found no Potter-Beckham docket, and PUCT Interchange documents returned HTTP 402 to automated fetch.

No OCC cause number exists yet for the Oklahoma segment. Transource expects to file its Certificate of Authority application in summer 2027, with a decision in late 2027 (fact-sheet graphic: 'FALL - WINTER 2027 OCC Approval').

No SPP Notification to Construct naming SPS or Transource Oklahoma for Beckham County-Potter was found (web search of spp.org, 2026-09-26). The Nov 4, 2025 minutes direct SPP staff to issue an NTC to the DTO. SPP-NTC-220936 (SPS, Oct 17, 2025, cached) covers Potter-Crossroads-Phantom 765 kV. Its 'Potter County 345 kV Substation Expansion' (named p.9; specification p.10: 'for the addition of three new 345 kV lines') sits beside three Tecovas-Potter County 345 kV circuits (pp.10-11). Whether any Beckham line terminal work at Potter is included is not stated.

Whole-line length conflicts across sources: 125 mi (Xcel information sheet, Transource page and fact sheet; also the sum of the 110 + 15 mi segment lengths on the Xcel page, which does not itself state 125), ~128 mi (Nov 21, 2025 Xcel and Transource releases) and ~150 mi (SPP IEP report, Oct 14, 2025, PDF p.9). The segment lengths (110 mi TX, 15 mi OK) agree between the utilities.

Whole-project cost conflicts: $222 million in the utility releases, matching Proposal B's RFP Response Estimate of $222,551,930 in SPP IEP Table 3 (PDF p.11), versus SPP's study cost estimate of $423,983,009 (IEP PDF p.9). The IEP also records a Proposal B-1 cost-overrun penalty threshold of $214.5 million (p.50). No source splits the cost between the Texas and Oklahoma segments.

The SPP IEP report splits winning Proposal B into B-1 (89% of the project) and B-2 (11%) without naming them. The split is consistent with SPS 110 mi / Transource 15 mi, but no source states the mapping.

The owning Transource entity is named inconsistently: 'Transource Energy LLC' (Xcel page), 'Transource Energy, LLC' (award releases) and 'Transource Oklahoma, LLC' (SPP minutes, as the bidder). The owner is recorded as Transource Oklahoma, LLC.

The Texas-Oklahoma crossing point is undetermined: neither state has a final route, and Transource's map shows several preliminary crossing links. The mapped state-line point is a county-edge placeholder (midpoint of Beckham County's western boundary, +/-27 km), not a sourced point.

The Xcel schedule (construction Q3 2028-Q4 2029, in-service Q4 2029) is published for 'the Project' on SPS's page and is not explicitly limited to the Texas portion. It is attributed to the SPS Texas package by inference.

Season-to-date conversion for the Transource construction window is a convention, not a sourced fact: Spring 2028 = 2028-03-01..2028-06-20 and Late 2028 = 2028-09-01..2028-12-31. Under these bounds the two construction windows overlap only as 'possible' (SPS starts in Q3 2028; Transource ends late 2028). The overlap becomes 'confirmed' only if 'Late 2028' is read as starting on or after 2028-09-30.

Schedule gap: the Transource timeline shows Oklahoma construction ending late 2028 but in-service in late 2029. Xcel shows construction from Q3 2028 to Q4 2029 with in-service in Q4 2029. The sources do not explain the Oklahoma gap, and whole-line energization timing should not be inferred.

Not modeled as construction windows: Transource's 'EARLY 2028 Right-of-Way Acquisition' (a milestone with no end date), 'SPRING 2027 Final Line Route Determined' and 'FALL - WINTER 2027 OCC Approval'. Xcel's land acquisition (Q2 2027-Q2 2028) is kept as a 'preconstruction' window, so the two packages' pre-construction phases are not represented symmetrically.

In-service claims agree in substance: Q4 2029 (Xcel), Late 2029 (Transource OK), November 2029 (both Nov 2025 releases) and a November 2029 schedule guarantee from both Proposal B respondents in the SPP IEP report. The IEP table's 'November 12th, 2029' (p.51) belongs to Proposal A (NextEra), so it is not attributed to these packages.

The Beckham County substation is an existing OG&E facility, and OG&E is a third utility. No source documents OG&E terminal work or an OG&E package for this line. SPP-NTC-220965 (OG&E, Dec 19, 2025, cached) does not mention Beckham.

Resource sharing is unknown. Xcel's Nov 2025 release quotes an Xcel director saying the partnership combines 'expertise' and 'resources', but no source documents shared crews, equipment, procurement or joint construction scheduling. Coordination is recorded as known-joint (joint-initiative and interconnection-design), not resource-sharing.

SPP's IEP report calls this line a 'necessary companion project' to SPS's Potter-Crossroads-Phantom 765 kV line, and both involve the Potter County substation. That pairing has the same owner (SPS) and belongs in a separate cluster if the 765 kV project is added; it is not a cross-utility lead.

Transource's project web page shows its timeline as an SVG image with outlined text, which cannot be verified by script. It was viewed and matches the fact-sheet PDF, so all Transource schedule excerpts cite the fact sheet.

The Xcel information sheet's schedule graphic (Construction Q3 2028 - Q4 2029, In Service Q4 2029, '(Schedule is subject to change.)') is visible on PDF p.1. In the cached text, map glyph characters split it into fragments shorter than 8 words, so it is cited only in notes, not as an excerpt.
